newsitem.title: USA: Clinton starts vacation after strike comments.
newsitem.headline: Clinton starts vacation after strike comments.

text.p: President Clinton began his vacation Sunday after urging United Parcel Service and union negotiators to end the two-week strike at the package carrier before the day ended.

"It's clear that they're making progress in the talks between UPS and the Teamsters," Clinton said at the White House before boarding his helicopter to leave for a three-week vacation on the Massachusetts island of Martha's Vineyard.

"This strike is beginning to hurt not only the company but its employees and the people who depend on it and I think they ought to redouble their efforts to settle the strike and they ought to do it today," he said after a briefing by Labor Secretary Alexis Herman and White House aide Bruce Lindsey.

Clinton's first stop on his three-week vacation -- the longest of his presidency -- was Block Island, a vacation spot off the coast of Rhode Island, before flying on to Martha's Vineyard this evening.

The president, accompanied by first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, their daughter Chelsea and Rebecca Kolsky, Chelsea's classmate at Sidwell Friends School, was welcomed by a crowd of several hundred people and the island's first warden, or mayor, Kim Gaffords.
Clinton said it took him a moment to realize that the first warden was the highest elected official on the island.
"I thought I was about to be arrested or something," he joked.

Clinton said he was "just anxious to be here and have some fun," although he made no reference to speculation that the Clintons were on the island to attend the wedding of actress Barbra Streisand and actor James Brolin.
Asked before his departure from the White House if he was going to a wedding, Clinton smiled, threw back his head and rolled his eyes, but he made no comment.
There have been speculative published reports that Streisand and Brolin would wed on Block Island this month and that Clinton might attend their wedding.
Clinton told the crowd that he hoped all of them would "always be committed to preserving this beautiful island."
He went on to say while economic expansion was important "we have to do it in a way that preserves the natural heritage that God has given us."
The Clintons planned to spend several hours on Block Island, a scheduled stop to include viewing a historic lighthouse that was recently moved because of beach erosion at its orginal site.
At Martha's Vineyard, White House aides have said the president plans to read, take walks and play golf.
He was scheduled to return to Washington Sunday, Sept. 7.
